resources.name: ConsentBasis
resources.doc:
The basis a policy stands on where one is required. Recorded, never inferred, and never
interpreted here: this package does not decide whether a basis is lawful.

resources.name: ConsentCounterparty
resources.doc:
Who the permission runs to, when it is not simply this controller. A keyed handle rather
than a universal entity reference: the domain resolves its own typed counterparty.

resources.name: ConsentDisposition
resources.doc:
Withdrawal, expiry by supersession, or narrowing. One terminal fact per grant, carrying
both axes: `effectiveAt` is when permission stopped applying, `recordedAt` is when we were
told. History is never erased — a withdrawn grant remains, which is what makes it possible
to answer what was permitted at the time something happened.

resources.name: ConsentEvidence
resources.doc:
How the grant was captured, kept separate so an unevidenced grant is still a recorded
fact rather than a missing one.

resources.name: ConsentPurpose
resources.doc:
Why the processing happens. Deliberately a separate axis from the activity: the same
activity can be consented for one purpose and refused for another.

resources.name: ConsentScope
resources.doc: Which data or resources are in scope.

resources.name: ProcessingActivity
resources.doc:
What is actually done. Storing, sharing, profiling and contacting are different acts and
a subject may agree to one without agreeing to another.

dataClasses.name: ConsentNarrative
dataClasses.doc:
Whether a subject agreed, to what, for how long, and how we know.

Consent is not authorization. A policy engine may read these facts to decide a request,
but nothing here grants access, and a missing grant is not a denial reason by itself —
it is the absence of one input. Consent is also not an agreement, an entitlement or a
notification preference: an unsubscribed newsletter says nothing about research consent,
and a contract that permits processing is a different fact with a different lifecycle.

Two time axes, both explicit. `validFrom`/`validUntil` is when the subject's permission
applies; `recordedAt` is when this instance learned of it. They differ whenever a paper
form is entered late or a withdrawal is backdated, and a decision made last Tuesday has to
be explainable with what was known last Tuesday rather than what is known now. These are
ordinary fields, a bounded interpretation rather than an L0 temporal facet: ConceptIR #75
is what would make valid and knowledge time a language-level axis.

classification.business: declared domain errors: served, counted separately
classification.counting: one event per logical operation; retries are attempts on the same event, never new events
